audits.title: EP-306 Management of acute sigmoid diverticulitis in a district general hospital – a retrospective audit
audits.standard: European Society of Coloproctology 2020 guidelines (including no routine antibiotics)
audits.setting: Emergency general surgery, Kingston Hospital NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 97% had CT and 100% received IV antibiotics; only 57% referred for outpatient lower GI endoscopy.

audits.other_findings: Mean length of stay 3.7 days for uncomplicated vs 9.3 days for complicated disease, suggesting a role for ambulatory care.
audits.citation: Egbe A. EP-306 Management of acute sigmoid diverticulitis in a district general hospital – a retrospective audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac245.081.

audits.title: SP4.1.2 Management and Ambulation of Uncomplicated Acute Diverticulitis during the COVID-19 Pandemic – A Clinical Audit in a District General Hospital
audits.standard: NICE-derived criteria for appropriate admission with acute uncomplicated diverticulitis
audits.setting: District general hospital general surgical department (Ealing Hospital, London)

cycle1.result: 14/18 (77.8%) admitted; 11 of 14 admitted and 15 of 18 overall could have been safely ambulated under national guidelines.

audits.other_findings: Inappropriate admissions stayed a mean of 3.27 days (49 avoidable patient-days), estimated at £78,400 per year; none needed surgery.
audits.citation: . SP4.1.2 Management and Ambulation of Uncomplicated Acute Diverticulitis during the COVID-19 Pandemic – A Clinical Audit in a District General Hospital. Br J Surg. 2022;109(Suppl 5).

audits.title: eP24 Streamlining Diverticulitis Care: An Audit of Hospital Admission Practices
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on diverticulitis (admission, antibiotics, dietary advice, outpatient colonoscopy)
audits.setting: Surgical teams in A&E across two centres, Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline figures not reported in abstract.

audits.intervention: Findings presented at M&M and teaching sessions, and posters across the department.

cycle2.result: Dietary advice increased by 57.8%; outpatient colonoscopy requests rose by 30.7%; no reduction in IV antibiotic use for uncomplicated diverticulitis.

audits.other_findings: Admissions after intervention correlated with significant comorbidities, consistent with NICE guidance.
audits.citation: de Andres Crespo M, Wubetu J, Dilaver N, Boulton R. eP24 Streamlining Diverticulitis Care: An Audit of Hospital Admission Practices. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae318.019.

audits.title: TPT 3.04 Acute Diverticulitis: An Audit of Management Against NICE Guidelines
audits.standard: NICE NG147 for antibiotic prescribing and surgical management of diverticular disease
audits.setting: Single district general hospital, Kingston Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Blood tests and CT imaging in 100%; antibiotic prescribing compliant with NICE in 38% (10/26); antibiotic duration 3–42 days, median 8 days.

audits.other_findings: Complications in 35% (9/26), 89% (8/9) managed conservatively; no abscess (n=3) had IR drainage as judged not feasible. Educational intervention and re-audit planned for February–March 2026.
audits.citation: Huseyin A, de Andres Crespo M. TPT 3.04 Acute Diverticulitis: An Audit of Management Against NICE Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.187.

audits.title: Should diverticulitis be managed in primary care? An audit on the management of diverticulitis in primary care.
audits.standard: NICE guidance on management of diverticulitis, including review within 48 hours

cycle1.result: Antibiotics prescribed after 68.4% (n = 39) of consultations; inflammatory markers in 19.3% (n = 11); review within 48 hours in only 3.5% (n = 2); referral to surgical assessment unit 12.5% (n = 8).

audits.other_findings: Only 3.5% (n = 2) deteriorated and needed admission; antibiotic regimen choice needs improvement.
audits.citation: Kiandee M, Sripada R. Should diverticulitis be managed in primary care? An audit on the management of diverticulitis in primary care. Br J Gen Pract. 2020;70(suppl 1):bjgp20X711665. doi:10.3399/bjgp20x711665. PMID: 32554687.
